title: Stuffed cabbage rolls
subtitle: American-Eastern-European beef-and-rice rolls in tomato sauce
excerpt: Blanched cabbage leaves wrapped around a well-seasoned beef-and-rice filling, braised in a sweet-and-sour tomato sauce until tender. A staple of American Midwest home cooking, brought by Eastern European immigrants in the early twentieth century.
sourceNotes: Stuffed cabbage rolls (known as gołąbki in Polish, golubki in Russian, töltött káposzta in Hungarian) were brought to the American Midwest by Polish, Hungarian, Czech, Slovak, and Russian Jewish immigrants between the 1880s and 1920s. The Americanised version with a sweet-and-sour tomato sauce appears in American community cookbooks from the early twentieth century. Joy of Cooking (1931) includes a version. The dish is now considered native to Midwestern American home cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely in the sauce and freeze. Defrost overnight and reheat gently.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Reheat gently in the oven at 160°C for 30 minutes.

content.text: Stuffed cabbage rolls are a project, but not a complicated one. The filling is easy to assemble; the blanching of the cabbage takes a few minutes; the rolling is satisfying; and then the oven does the work for 90 minutes while the sauce reduces around the rolls. The sweet-and-sour tomato sauce is the Americanisation of the dish: the Eastern European originals are more savoury. Both are good.

Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Lower the whole cabbage into the water and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the outer leaves are pliable. Pull off leaves as they soften and drain on a tea towel. You need 12 to 14 large leaves. Trim the thick central rib from each leaf so it rolls more easily.
Mix all the filling ingredients together until combined. Heat the oven to 170°C (fan 150°C). Mix the sauce ingredients together.

Place 2 to 3 tablespoons of filling at the base of a cabbage leaf. Fold the sides in, then roll up tightly. Repeat. Spread a third of the sauce in a deep baking dish. Arrange the rolls in a single layer, seam-side down. Pour the remaining sauce over and around the rolls.

Cover tightly with foil and bake for 1.5 hours until the rolls are tender and the filling is cooked through. Remove the foil for the last 20 minutes. Taste the sauce and adjust the sweet-sour balance with more sugar or lemon juice.

items.symptom: Rolls fall apart in the sauce
items.cause: Not rolled tightly enough, or seam not tucked under
items.fix: Ensure the seam is facing down in the baking dish. Use cocktail sticks to secure if needed, removing before serving.

content.text: Stuffed cabbage rolls are Midwestern American immigrant food. Polish, Hungarian, Russian, and Balkan communities brought them to Chicago, Cleveland, Detroit, Pittsburgh, and the steel towns of western Pennsylvania. The great waves of Eastern European immigration ran from 1880 to 1920. Every community has its own version, known as gołąbki, golabki, halupki, golumpki, or simply stuffed cabbage. Every family has its own recipe within that. The sweet-and-sour tomato sauce is the Americanisation that most versions share.
